comment:
One configuration-preservation regression found at `f7105b5a`: the Quattro upgrade overwrites customized Bluetooth policy, although the new standalone migration preserves it.

### Quattro upgrade replaces customized Bluetooth configuration

The new [`config/` copy](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f7105b5ae2d98e87abda25abf499aa2fe0219484/bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro#L2089-L2094) unconditionally replaces `~/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/bluetooth-a2dp-autoconnect.conf`. The earlier missing-file seeding preserves existing files, and this Bluetooth file is not in the upgrade's hash-based refresh list. The old `default/` branch does not run with either pinned tree's layout; adding the current path makes the overwrite reachable.

A synthetic customized file already using only `a2dp_sink`, with a device-specific match and `bluez5.hw-volume = [ ]`, produced this comparison using extracted production upgrade helpers and the copy block:

| Path | Custom device match and hardware-volume setting |
| --- | --- |
| Base upgrade code | Preserved |
| Head migration alone | Preserved |
| Head upgrade code | Replaced by stock policy, without a per-file backup |
| Head migration after that copy | Does not restore the lost settings |

**Impact:** users with custom rules in this shipped file lose their active Bluetooth policy during the Quattro transition, including configurations that already exclude `a2dp_source`.

**Suggested change:** remove the extra copy or preserve existing files there. `copy_missing_config_defaults` already installs the current default when the file is absent, and migration `1790015500` can update exact old-stock copies later without overwriting customizations. Apply the same distinction to any retained legacy fallback.

**Verified:** the standalone migration updates exact stock copies, preserves custom and missing files, is idempotent, avoids starting an inactive service, and retains restart state after a modeled failure so a later invocation retries successfully. The added migration test's six assertions also passed.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned base/head source inspection and isolated file-behavior tests with a stubbed `systemctl`. Upgrade coverage used extracted production code, not a full system upgrade; broader snapshot recovery was not tested. No Bluetooth hardware, native WirePlumber crash prevention, or downstream shell recovery was verified.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Opus 5 and Astra technical reviews, followed by Astra synthesis and verification of the public claims against targeted evidence.
